From: Alan Cho <alan@nimblepay.com>

Date: 2026-12-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: High error rate / latency on Dec 16 - request for credit

Hi Sean,

We saw a major spike in latency and 5xx errors on Dec 16 between 02:10-03:40 UTC which affected our payment flow (retries spiked, ~18% failed authorizations for that window). Our infra and product teams have the incident report attached. This impacted an estimated $1.2M in attempted transactions and caused customer support volume to increase significantly.

Per our contract SLOs (99.9% availability, 200ms p90 latency) this clearly exceeded tolerances and we'd like to discuss remediation and a fair concession. Can you propose a compensation structure (credit amount or free service months) and next steps for documentation/legal? NimblePay needs a written concession offer we can route to our procurement and legal teams.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we have a renewal review on Jan 8 and would like this resolved beforehand.

Thanks,
Alan Cho
Head of Platform
NimblePay

Alan — thanks for the note and the report. I'm very sorry NimblePay hit that window; I appreciate you documenting the impact.

I've looped in our customer success and finance leads to evaluate the right remedy and get you a written concession. Quick plan:

Team —

Summary: NimblePay (enterprise, renews Jan 8) had a service incident on 2026-12-16 that produced prolonged high latency and an estimated 18% failure in payment authorizations for a ~90-minute window. Customer is requesting a written concession before their renewal. Incident report and initial calc attached.

Proposed options to offer (pick one; each requires sign-off):
1) One-time service credit of $25,000 applied to next invoice + formal apology and 6-month SLO monitoring assistance.
2) Two months of waived platform fees (consumption up to their historical monthly average) — approximate value $28k — requires Accounting to confirm recognition.
3) Proportional usage credit equal to 30% of Dec invoice (estimated $18,000) + a goodwill $5k remediation credit.

Recommendation: Offer #3 capped at $22,000 to balance customer relationship and precedents. We should include a short term SLO gate (free elevated support for 60 days) as non-financial remediation.

Ask: Marissa — approve the customer-relations goodwill offer (non-standard concession). Karthik — legal/discount approval for up to $30k? Laura — finance sign-off if we cap at $22k and how to present on next invoice.

I will draft the concession letter and the DocuSign packet once we align.

Thanks,
Sean
